data.notes:
Course description (verbatim): In the current highly mediatized world (see the work of Andreas Hepp), the popular media’s image of the city hardly represents the majority of citizens’ everyday city experiences or perceptions of their future. The misrepresentation of urban conditions in media on one side creates processes of visibility and invisibility for the city among not only the general public but also urban experts who get enrolled in the process of producing these city/ies (images). On the other side, it affect and facilitates marginalization, disablement as well as socio-spatial injustices and the further exclusion of vulnerable groups from services and infrastructure. In many cities worldwide, these vulnerable groups form the majority of the population. In this seminar, I suggest that the corresponding visual representation and consequent misrepresentation of socio-spatial conditions in cities can be termed as 'Visual in/Justice'. This seminar to make visible the intersection of social and spatial in/justice in the current highly mediatized world.

Biography (verbatim): Mennatullah Hendawy is a Research Associate and PhD Candidate at the Chair of Urban Design, TU Berlin. She is also a Visiting Researcher at the Leibniz Institute for Research on Society and Space in Erkner, Germany and an affiliated Assistant Lecturer at the Department of Urban Planning and Design in Ain Shams University in Cairo, Egypt. Mennatullah works on the intersection of urban planning, mediatisation, and justice where she is fascinated by the way knowledge, power, and agency are man-fested in and co-construct cities and the public sphere.
